title: Introduce Density Inspector with Predictive Column Summaries
creator: Priya Nambiar
description:
Problem: Customers frequently switch density modes (comfortable/compact/condensed) and then manually resize or hide columns to fit critical data. Our current table controls are buried in menus, offer no cross-column preview, and provide little guidance on when to choose a density preset vs. manual compression. This causes friction during analysis workflows and increases support requests about column discoverability.

Proposal: Add a Density Inspector — a contextual panel surfaced from the table header that provides: a) predictive column summaries (estimated visible width and information density per column based on recent user interactions and sample row data), b) an interactive visualizer showing how different density presets affect row height and column truncation, c) one-click apply for suggested presets and column collapse order, and d) keyboard-first controls with ARIA announcements. The Inspector will be available on virtualized tables and coordinate with the runtime by exposing a minimal telemetry hook to estimate tokenized cell widths for better predictions.

Scope: UI/UX design + interaction spec, accessibility annotations, telemetry event definitions, handoff tokens (spacing/line-height), a small prototype in Figma and a lightweight interactive HTML prototype for engineering to test with our virtualization harness. Not included: full analytics dashboard work or backend indexing of all customer tables (we will start with sampling on-client and conservative heuristics).
acceptance_criteria: Density Inspector mockups completed for desktop/tablet screens and reviewed by PM and Eng (Figma link referenced).
Interactive prototype demonstrates: predictive column summaries, density preview, and one-click apply for density presets.
Accessibility: keyboard navigation, ARIA announcements for density changes, and screen-reader walkthrough documented.
Design tokens (spacing/line-height/font-size) updated with migration notes and included in the handoff spec.

design_decisions: Predictive summaries will use client-side sampling + heuristic width estimator instead of server-side indexing to avoid PII and backend scope expansion.
Density presets will be first-class (Comfortable, Balanced, Compact) and exposed as quick actions; advanced manual compression will remain in the column menu.

We will prioritize keyboard and screen-reader flows; Inspector can be invoked via keyboard shortcut (press \ to open focus search then 'D' to open inspector) and will provide live ARIA region updates when applying presets.
Telemetry events will be minimal: user_open_inspector, apply_density_preset, manual_column_collapse; no raw cell contents will be logged.
testing_plan: Prototype usability with 3 power-user sessions (metrics: time-to-configure, number of manual resizes avoided).
A/B canary in 5% of internal beta customers to measure reduction in manual column-resize actions and support tickets related to table layout.
Accessibility audit by D&I team and automated checks (axe-core) on the interactive prototype.
Performance test with virtualization harness (ENG-3012) to ensure inspector sampling does not add >8ms median render time on 95th percentile large tables.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Design review sign-off and prototype handoff (target: 2025-06-20).
Phase 2: Engineering spike and client-side sampling integration (ENG-3012), internal canary for Desktop web (2 weeks).
Phase 3: 5% external canary, collect usage metrics and user feedback, iterate on copy and affordances.
Phase 4: Full release behind feature flag with opt-out and telemetry gating; include migration notes for teams that consume table tokens.
